what_happened: The job "Hold jobs on low disk after cleanup; default 10G minimum free" (20261017-001109-qfax) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic confirmed the named functions exist and that most criteria had demonstrations that would fail without the behavior. It raised one major finding. A hold just before the checks leaves the job Dispatched, and the plan left the resume route as an open question for the producer. The only existing resume path for such a job is `athena retry`, which creates a new job and leaves the held job Dispatched with its marker never cleared. So criterion 3(b) could not be shown for the held job. There were also three minor findings. state.rs and status.rs are not in the reading's deliverables. The drain tests only stub `Run { held: true }` and never show that `RealSteps::run` maps a real LowDisk error to held. NeedsAccepting ends the item's work, so a verification-stage hold reappears only on a later drain, and the plan did not say so. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage is not required to trace the full lifecycle of a new state (here a hold at each stage) through the existing resume, retry and drain paths. It may also leave a design question as "producer to decide", and nothing forbids that for a question that decides whether a criterion can be met. The critic is the first stage to read the real resume code, so the gap shows up only in the last round. The three-round cap keeps no partial plan, and a retry would start without the critic's findings. The reading also omitted the files the design needs (state.rs, status.rs), which cost rounds on minor findings. The closest registered class, plan-misses-external-service-state-precondition, is about external services. A better fit may be a new class, but the nearest in-pattern case is the earlier plan that left a consequence open as a "check" for the producer.
prevention: Add a planning-template rule: when a plan introduces a new job state or hold, it must list every way a job in that state leaves it (resume, retry, close, drain re-listing) with the existing function that does each, and may not leave any as an open question for the producer. The critic checks this before other points. Each such path needs a demonstration through the real step mapping, not a stub. The reading must list the state and status files the design touches. Also keep the critic's findings and the last plan, so a retry resumes from them and not from scratch.
proposed_request: Hold jobs on low disk after cleanup, with a default minimum of 10G free space. Outcome: when free disk is below the minimum after Athena's cleanup, a job is held instead of failed, at dispatch and also just before the checks. A held job must be resumable on its own: when space returns, the next drain picks up the same job, clears its hold marker and continues it, without making a new job. `athena retry` is not the resume route. Acceptance: (1) A dispatch-stage hold leaves the job Proposed and it runs on a later drain once space is free. (2) A hold just before the checks leaves the job Dispatched with a marker. A drain test goes through the real RealSteps::run mapping from a real LowDisk error to held, then shows the same job resumes and its marker is cleared after space returns. (3) The 10G default is in config with the digest reset, and the idle sweep respects job locks. (4) The plan states that a verification-stage hold reappears on a later drain through the interrupted-work listing, and tests that. Allowed files include crates/athena-core/src/state.rs and status.rs along with run.rs, drain.rs and the config, tests and changelog.
